question: Topical phenylephrine 2.5% causes the superficial inflamed vessels of episcleritis to blanch, whereas the deep scleral vessels of scleritis do not blanch.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Recall the phenylephrine test: episcleritis (superficial vessels) blanches; scleritis (deep vessels) does not.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Phenylephrine constricts the superficial episcleral plexus, so episcleritis blanches; the deeper scleral plexus in scleritis does not, which is the key bedside discriminator.
